status: in progress; overall throughput and memory parity not achieved
implementation: Published quinn 0.11.12 plus private endpoint-to-connection channel. Single endpoint-owned sender and connection-owned receiver; first event inline, overflow grows on demand, FIFO and close/rebind delivery retained. Tokio cooperative budget consumption retained via public poll_proceed (minimum Tokio 1.47, rt enabled; project uses 1.53.3). Oversized empty overflow buffers release after bursts; retention threshold matches the original mpsc block, 32 slots on 64-bit and 16 otherwise, with no queue-depth cap. Unwind cleanup recovers a poisoned queue lock to avoid a second panic. No wire, stream-credit, crypto or congestion-control changes.
scope: Local Linux loopback. Final comparisons: three alternating fresh-process runs per case/variant, four pinned server workers on CPUs 0-3, eight client workers on CPUs 8-15, four seconds, 1 KiB values, 32 private pairs, 1024 room readers, fanout window four. Same frozen independently verifying clients. Content, sender, FIFO, counters, departures/close and final gauges checked. Logarithmic latency percentiles are upper bounds. RSS is sampled at phase gates, excludes kernel socket memory, and differs from requested live heap or continuous peak.

validation.standalone_test_scope: All six changed files byte-identical to the vendor copy. Standalone lock explicitly selects the same patched quinn-proto 0.11.19 and Tokio 1.53.3 as the product; early prototype tests used the archive lock at 0.11.18 and are not cited as final pinned-graph evidence. Three window tests ignored by default were run explicitly and passed.
validation.vendor: 152 files verified against four original archives and three declared patches
validation.fixture_fix: Observed valid global broadcast preceding authentication ACK in legacy responsiveness test. Fixture now waits for the matching ACK while validating intervening non-control frames. Product ordering unchanged. Three targeted repetitions and full suite passed.
validation.browser: Chromium 155 actual delivered bundle passed all nine checks: typed values, private/broadcast, datagrams, 128 KiB/5 MiB payloads, variables, departure and genuine graceful close; seven final gauges zero.

initial_channel.scope: Early three-run prototype before explicit large-burst storage release; superseded for final claims.
initial_channel.finding: A 10000-item burst retained 16384 overflow slots after drain. Negative assertion also exposed poisoned-lock cleanup panicking during unwind. Both have final regression checks.

heap.scope: 8194 sessions, gperftools replacement allocator. Excluded from ordinary timing/RSS medians. Three original gates plus delayed observations at 1 and 5 seconds while the fully closed client is held at done.
heap.interpretation: Logical gauges reach zero before all asynchronous cleanup finishes. Requested live bytes fall further shortly afterwards; higher RSS cannot be treated as the same amount of live connection memory. Do not generalize the instrumented allocator RSS to production.

freshness_scope: One final candidate check per clean/loss/reorder mode. 360 offered 1 KiB states at 60 Hz over six seconds plus reliable 1 MiB bulk. Loss profile: 20 ms one-way and 2% packet loss; reorder additionally 8 ms jitter and 25% reordering. External port only, both directions, temporary isolated namespace; TLS proxy internal hop unimpaired. Same seeds/parameters are not identical packet-loss trajectories. Probes include initial state before first update; stale sequences cannot replace new state. Unreceived updates are not attributed exclusively to network loss. Single samples do not establish statistical protocol rankings.
remaining: Memory and room/mixed throughput remain behind the plaintext control, and mixed private traffic remains behind the encrypted fixture. Continue active connection/task storage and reliable fairness work. Observer cancellation/re-subscribe, full concurrent 100k/8192 inspection, broader overload/shutdown, QUIC buffer accounting and final packaging/deployment documentation remain required. No acceptance or release claim.
